posts.title: Community Medicine for UPSC CMS: Demography, Health Indicators and National Programs Deep Dive
posts.description: Community medicine for UPSC CMS — demography (birth rate, death rate, growth rate), health indicators (IMR, MMR, HDI), and national programs in detail.
posts.excerpt: Community medicine for UPSC CMS — demography, health indicators, and national programs with targets, implementing agencies, and recent updates.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Demography

**Crude Birth Rate:** Live births per 1000 population per year.
**Crude Death Rate:** Deaths per 1000 population per year.
**Growth Rate:** Birth rate - Death rate + Net migration.
**Total Fertility Rate:** Average number of children per woman.
**Replacement Level:** TFR of 2.1.

## Health Indicators

**IMR:** Deaths under 1 year per 1000 live births. India: ~28 (2023).
**MMR:** Maternal deaths per 100,000 live births. India: ~97 (2018-20).
**NMR:** Neonatal deaths per 1000 live births.
**U5MR:** Under-5 deaths per 1000 live births.

posts.title: PSM Biostatistics Formulas for UPSC CMS: The Complete Reference With Solved PYQs
posts.description: PSM biostatistics formulas for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, relative risk, odds ratio, Chi-square, t-test with PYQ examples.
posts.excerpt: PSM biostatistics formulas for UPSC CMS — sensitivity, specificity, RR, OR, Chi-square, t-test with solved PYQ examples and formula cheat sheet.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Key Formulas

**Sensitivity** = TP / (TP + FN)
**Specificity** = TN / (TN + FP)
**PPV** = TP / (TP + FP)
**NPV** = TN / (TN + FN)

**Relative Risk (RR)** = [a/(a+b)] / [c/(c+d)] — incidence in exposed vs unexposed
**Odds Ratio (OR)** = (a x d) / (b x c) — odds of exposure in cases vs controls

**Chi-square** = sum((O-E)2/E) — test of independence
**t-test** = (Mean1 - Mean2) / SE — compare two means

posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Lymphoma Classification

**Hodgkin:** Reed-Sternberg cells (CD15+, CD30+). Nodular sclerosis (young females), Mixed cellularity, Lymphocyte-rich, Lymphocyte-depleted.

**Non-Hodgkin:**
- B-cell: DLBCL (most common), Follicular, Mantle cell, Burkitt (starry sky), Marginal zone
- T-cell: PTCL-NOS, AITL, ALCL

## Multiple Myeloma

CRAB: hyperCalcemia, Renal insufficiency, Anaemia, Bone lesions (lytic). Serum protein electrophoresis: M-spike. Treatment: Bortezomib + Lenalidomide + Dexamethasone.

posts.title: Forensic Medicine Identification for UPSC CMS: DNA, Fingerprints, Dental and Age Estimation
posts.description: Forensic medicine identification for UPSC CMS — DNA profiling, fingerprint classification, dental identification, age estimation, and the medicolegal procedures.
posts.excerpt: Forensic medicine identification for UPSC CMS — DNA, fingerprints, dental records, age estimation from bones/teeth, and the medicolegal identification methods.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## DNA Profiling

Most accurate identification method. STR analysis. Match probability: 1 in several billion. Used in paternity, criminal cases, disaster victim identification.

## Fingerprint Classification

Loops (60%), Whorls (30%), Arches (10%). Permanent from birth. Even identical twins have different fingerprints.

## Dental Identification

Most reliable in fire/advanced decomposition. Compare ante-mortem and post-mortem dental records. Dental pulp DNA if needed.

## Age Estimation

**Dental:** Nolla stages (children), secondary dentin deposition (adults), root translucency (aging).
**Skeletal:** Epiphyseal fusion, pubic symphysis, sternal rib ends, dental wear.

posts.title: Forensic Medicine Toxicology for UPSC CMS: Common Poisons, Antidotes and Post-Mortem Signs
posts.description: Forensic medicine toxicology for UPSC CMS — organophosphates, heavy metals, barbiturates, alcohols, common poisons with antidotes and autopsy findings.
posts.excerpt: Forensic medicine toxicology for UPSC CMS — common poisons, antidotes, post-mortem signs, and the toxicology facts tested every year.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Common Poisons

**Organophosphates:** SLUDGE symptoms, miosis, fasciculations. Antidote: Atropine + PAM.

**Heavy metals:**
- Arsenic: Garlic breath, rice-water stools, Mees lines
- Mercury: Erethism, gingivitis, tremors
- Lead: Burton line (blue gum line), abdominal colic, anemia

**Barbiturates:** CNS depression, coma, respiratory depression. No specific antidote. Supportive care.

**Alcohol:** Ethanol (depression, odor, hypoglycemia), Methanol (visual disturbances, formate toxicity - treat with ethanol/fomepizole).

posts.title: Surgery Trauma for UPSC CMS: ATLS, Abdominal Trauma, Burns and Polytrauma Management
posts.description: Surgery trauma for UPSC CMS — ATLS primary survey, abdominal trauma assessment, burn classification and management, and polytrauma priorities.
posts.excerpt: Surgery trauma for UPSC CMS — ATLS primary survey, abdominal trauma, burn management, and polytrauma priorities that every Medical Officer must know.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## ATLS Primary Survey

A: Airway with C-spine
B: Breathing (chest X-ray, chest tube if hemopneumothorax)
C: Circulation (2 large-bore IVs, fluid resuscitation, pelvic binder)
D: Disability (GCS, pupils)
E: Exposure (log roll, examine back)

## Abdominal Trauma

**Blunt:** FAST scan (Focused Assessment with Sonography for Trauma). Positive = emergency laparotomy.
**Penetrating:** Gunshot (explore all), Stab (selective management).

## Burns

Rule of Nines: Head 9%, each arm 9%, each leg 18%, anterior trunk 18%, posterior trunk 18%, perineum 1%.
Fluid resuscitation: Parkland formula (4mL x %TBSA x weight in kg) = 50% in first 8 hours.

posts.title: Critical Care Medicine for UPSC CMS: Ventilator Settings, Inotropes and ICU Scoring Systems
posts.description: Critical care medicine for UPSC CMS — ventilator settings, inotropes/vasopressors, ICU scoring systems (APACHE, SOFA), fluid resuscitation, and the critical care facts tested.
posts.excerpt: Critical care medicine for UPSC CMS — ventilator modes, inotropes, ICU scoring systems, fluid resuscitation, and the critical care knowledge tested in exams.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Ventilator Settings

**AC (Assist-Control):** Set RR, VT (6-8 mL/kg PBW), PEEP (5), FiO2 (titrate to SpO2 >92%).
**SIMV:** Synchronized intermittent mandatory ventilation.
**PS (Pressure Support):** Patient-triggered, pressure-limited.
**CPAP:** Continuous positive airway pressure (spontaneous breathing).

## Inotropes/Vasopressors

| Drug | Mechanism | Dose | Effect |
|------|-----------|------|--------|
| Norepinephrine | Alpha + Beta-1 | 0.01-0.5 mcg/kg/min | Vasoconstriction |
| Dopamine | Dose-dependent | 2-20 mcg/kg/min | Dose-dependent |
| Dobutamine | Beta-1 | 2-20 mcg/kg/min | Inotropy |
| Vasopressin | V1 receptor | 0.03 U/min | Vasoconstriction |

## Scoring Systems

APACHE II: Age + 12 acute physiologic variables + chronic health + surgical status.

posts.title: Advanced Rheumatology for UPSC CMS: Vasculitis, Spondyloarthropathy and Connective Tissue Disorders
posts.description: Advanced rheumatology for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — ANCA vasculitis, spondyloarthropathy (ankylosing spondylitis, PsA, ReA), scleroderma, Sjogren, and mixed connective tissue disease.
posts.excerpt: Advanced rheumatology for UPSC CMS — ANCA vasculitis, spondyloarthropathy, scleroderma, MCTD, with autoantibody panels and treatment algorithms.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Spondyloarthropathy

Shared features: Inflammatory back pain, enthesitis, peripheral arthritis, dactylitis, extra-articular (uveitis, psoriasis, IBD), HLA-B27 association.

**Ankylosing Spondylitis:** Bamboo spine, sacroiliitis. Treatment: NSAIDs, Physiotherapy, TNF inhibitors.

**Psoriatic Arthritis:** Dactylitis, sausage digits, pencil-in-cup on X-ray. Treatment: NSAIDs, DMARDs, biologics.

**Reactive Arthritis:** Post-infectious (Chlamydia, GI). Conjunctivitis, Urethritis, Arthritis triad. Self-limiting.

## Systemic Sclerosis

Skin thickening, Raynaud's, esophageal dysmotility, pulmonary fibrosis, scleroderma renal crisis.

posts.title: Systemic Pathology for UPSC CMS: Vasculitis, Shock, Transplant Rejection and Immunopathology
posts.description: Systemic pathology for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — vasculitis types, shock pathology, transplant rejection types, amyloidosis, and systemic disease mechanisms.
posts.excerpt: Systemic pathology for UPSC CMS — vasculitis classification, transplant rejection types, amyloidosis, and the systemic mechanisms that underlie disease.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Vasculitis by Vessel Size

**Large vessel:** Giant cell (temporal) arteritis, Takayasu.
**Medium vessel:** PAN, Kawasaki.
**Small vessel (ANCA-associated):** GPA, MPA, EGPA.
**Small vessel (immune complex):** IgA vasculitis (Henoch-Schonlein), Cryoglobulinemia.

## Transplant Rejection

**Hyperacute:** Minutes. ABO mismatch. Pre-formed antibodies.
**Acute:** Days-weeks. T-cell mediated. Treat with steroids.
**Chronic:** Months-years. Obliterative vasculopathy.

## Amyloidosis

AA (secondary, chronic inflammation), AL (primary, myeloma), ATTR (transthyretin, familial). Congo red staining -> apple-green birefringence.

posts.title: General Pathology for UPSC CMS: Cell Injury, Inflammation, Immunity and Neoplasia
posts.description: General pathology for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — cell injury, inflammation, immunity, neoplasia, and the pathology concepts tested as clinical vignettes.
posts.excerpt: General pathology for UPSC CMS — cell injury, inflammation, immunity, neoplasia, and the pathology concepts tested as the basis of clinical vignettes.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Cell Injury

Reversible: Cell swelling, fatty change. Irreversible: Nuclear changes (pyknosis, karyorrhexis, karyolysis), membrane damage, Myelin figures.

## Inflammation

Acute: Neutrophils, edema, fibrin. Chronic: Lymphocytes, plasma cells, macrophages, fibroblasts. Granulomatous: Epithelioid cells, Langhans giant cells, caseous necrosis (TB).

## Neoplasia

Benign: Well-differentiated, encapsulated, slow-growing, no metastasis.
Malignant: Poorly differentiated, invasive, fast-growing, metastasis.

Oncogenes: c-myc, ras, HER2. Tumor suppressor: p53, Rb.

posts.title: Abdominal Radiology for UPSC CMS: X-Ray, Ultrasound and CT Signs You Must Know
posts.description: Abdominal radiology for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — abdominal X-ray signs (Rigler, coffee bean), ultrasound findings, CT signs, and the imaging appearances tested.
posts.excerpt: Abdominal radiology for UPSC CMS — X-ray signs, ultrasound findings, CT appearances, and the imaging-based questions that appear every year.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Abdominal X-Ray Signs

**Rigler sign:** Both walls of bowel visible = pneumoperitoneum.
**Coffee bean sign:** Sigmoid volvulus.
**Hausser sign:** Multiple air-fluid levels = small bowel obstruction.
**Hepatic flexure sign:** Large bowel obstruction.

## Ultrasound Findings

**Gallstones:** Echogenic with posterior acoustic shadowing.
**Cholecystitis:** Gallbladder wall thickening (>3mm), pericholecystic fluid, sonographic Murphy sign.
**Hydronephrosis:** Dilated renal pelvis and calyces.
**Free fluid:** Morrison's pouch, splenorenal recess.

posts.title: Chest X-Ray Interpretation for UPSC CMS: 15 Signs and Patterns Every Aspirant Must Recognize
posts.description: Chest X-ray interpretation for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — 15 key signs and patterns, systematic approach, and the chest X-ray appearances that appear as image questions.
posts.excerpt: Chest X-ray interpretation for UPSC CMS — 15 key signs and patterns, systematic approach, and the appearances tested as image-based questions.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Systematic Approach (ABCDE)

**A**irways: Trachea midline/deviated. Endotracheal tube position.
**B**ones: Ribs, clavicles, scapulae, humeri. Fractures, lytic lesions.
**C**ardiac: Cardiac size (CTR <0.5), cardiac borders, aortic knuckle.
**D**iaphragm: Right higher than left, costophrenic angles sharp.
**E**verything else: Lung fields, mediastinum, hila.

## 15 Key Signs

1. Air bronchogram = consolidation
2. Bat wing = pulmonary edema
3. Silhouette sign = right middle lobe collapse
4. Honeycombing = interstitial lung disease
5. Cavity = TB, abscess, cancer
6. Coin lesion = granuloma vs cancer
7. Pleural effusion = blunted costophrenic angle
8. Pneumothorax = visceral pleural line, no vessels beyond

posts.title: Obstetric Anaesthesia for UPSC CMS: Labour Analgesia, GA for C-Section and Complications
posts.description: Obstetric anaesthesia for UPSC CMS — labour analgesia (epidural), GA for emergency C-section, pre-eclampsia considerations, and obstetric anaesthesia complications.
posts.excerpt: Obstetric anaesthesia for UPSC CMS — labour epidural, GA for C-section, pre-eclampsia management, aspiration risk, and complications.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Labour Analgesia

Epidural analgesia: Gold standard. Bupivacaine + Fentanyl via epidural catheter. Reduces maternal stress, improves fetal outcome.

## GA for Emergency C-Section

Rapid sequence induction (RSI): Pre-oxygenate -> Thiopentone/Propofol + Succinylcholine -> Cricoid pressure -> Intubate.

## Aspiration Risk (Mendelson Syndrome)

Pregnant women at risk from 2nd trimester. Empty stomach, antacid pre-medication, RSI, left lateral tilt.

## Pre-eclampsia

Avoid spinal hypotension: pre-load with crystalloid. Epidural preferred over spinal for labour.

posts.title: Orthopaedics Soft Tissue and Bone Tumours for UPSC CMS: Classification, Features and Management
posts.description: Orthopaedics soft tissue and bone tumors for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — benign vs malignant tumors, Enneking staging, common tumors, and the radiologic features.
posts.excerpt: Orthopaedics soft tissue and bone tumors for UPSC CMS — benign vs malignant, Enneking staging, common bone tumors with radiologic features and management.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Bone Tumor Classification

**Benign:** Osteoma, Osteoid osteoma, Osteochondroma, Enchondroma, Giant cell tumor, Aneurysmal bone cyst.

**Malignant:** Osteosarcoma, Chondrosarcoma, Ewing sarcoma, Fibrosarcoma.

## Common Bone Tumors

**Osteosarcoma:** Most common primary malignant bone tumor. Adolescents, metaphysis of long bones (distal femur). X-ray: sunburst appearance, Codman triangle. Treatment: Neo-adjuvant chemo + surgery + adjuvant chemo.

**Ewing Sarcoma:** Children, diaphysis of long bones. X-ray: onion-skin periosteal reaction. Treatment: Chemo + surgery/radiotherapy.

## Enneking Staging

Stage I: Low grade (intracompartmental A, extracompartmental B).
Stage II: High grade (intracompartmental A, extracompartmental B).
Stage III: Metastatic.

posts.title: Orthopaedics Arthritis for UPSC CMS: OA, RA, Gout, Septic Arthritis and Crystal Arthropathy
posts.description: Orthopaedics arthritis for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — OA, RA, gout, pseudogout, septic arthritis, with clinical features, investigations, and management.
posts.excerpt: Arthritis types for UPSC CMS — OA, RA, gout, septic arthritis with joint findings, synovial fluid analysis, crystal identification, and treatment.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Osteoarthritis

Most common arthritis. Weight-bearing joints (knee, hip, spine). Heberden nodes (DIP), Bouchard nodes (PIP). X-ray: joint space narrowing, osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis. Treatment: NSAIDs, physiotherapy, joint replacement.

## Rheumatoid Arthritis

Symmetrical small joint involvement. Morning stiffness >1hr. X-ray: periarticular osteopenia, marginal erosions, joint space narrowing. Treatment: DMARDs.

## Crystal Arthropathy

**Gout:** Monosodium urate crystals. Needle-shaped, negatively birefringent. Podagra (1st MTP). Treatment: NSAIDs, Colchicine, Steroids, Allopurinol (long-term).

**Pseudogout:** Calcium pyrophosphate dihydrate. Rhomboid, positively birefringent. Knee most common.

posts.title: Local and Regional Anaesthesia for UPSC CMS: Types, Indications, Complications and Drug Doses
posts.description: Local and regional anaesthesia for UPSC CMS — local anaesthetics, spinal, epidural, brachial plexus block, indications, complications, and drug doses.
posts.excerpt: Local and regional anaesthesia for UPSC CMS — local anaesthetic types, spinal, epidural, nerve blocks, complications, and the drug doses tested.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Local Anaesthetics

**Amide type:** Lidocaine, Bupivacaine, Ropivacaine. Metabolized in liver.
**Ester type:** Procaine, Chloroprocaine, Cocaine. Metabolized by pseudocholinesterase.

Mechanism: Block Na+ channels -> prevent depolarization.

## Spinal Anaesthesia

Lidocaine (short), Bupivacaine (long). Level depends on baricity, dose, patient position. Complications: hypotension, post-dural puncture headache, nerve damage.

## Epidural Anaesthesia

Catheter placed in epidural space. Used for labour analgesia, post-op analgesia, chronic pain. Can top-up as needed.

posts.title: Surgery Shock Types for UPSC CMS: Hypovolemic, Septic, Cardiogenic and Neurogenic
posts.description: Shock types for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — hypovolemic, septic (warm/cold), cardiogenic, neurogenic, anaphylactic with clinical features, investigations and management.
posts.excerpt: Shock types for UPSC CMS — hypovolemic, septic, cardiogenic, neurogenic, anaphylactic with distinguishing features, fluid resuscitation, and vasopressors.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Hypovolemic Shock

Causes: Hemorrhage, burns, diarrhea, vomiting, third spacing.
Features: Cold, clammy skin, tachycardia, hypotension, low JVP, oliguria.
Management: IV fluids (crystalloid first), blood if hemorrhagic, treat cause.

## Septic Shock

Warm shock (early): Warm, flushed skin, bounding pulse, wide pulse pressure. Cold shock (late): Cold, clammy, narrow pulse pressure.
Management: Fluids (30mL/kg), Antibiotics within 1 hour, Vasopressors (norepinephrine).

## Cardiogenic Shock

Low CO, high PCWP. Causes: Large MI, severe arrhythmia, valve rupture. Treatment: Inotropes (dobutamine, dopamine), afterload reduction, PCI.

## Neurogenic Shock

Loss of sympathetic tone. Warm, dry skin, hypotension, bradycardia.

posts.title: Gynaecologic Oncology for UPSC CMS: Cervical, Ovarian, Endometrial Cancer Staging and Management
posts.description: Gynaecologic oncology for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — cervical, ovarian, endometrial, vulval cancer with FIGO staging, risk factors, screening, and management.
posts.excerpt: Gynaecologic oncology for UPSC CMS — cervical, ovarian, endometrial, vulval cancer with FIGO staging, screening protocols, and treatment algorithms.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Cervical Cancer

Screening: Pap smear (cytology) + HPV testing. Starts at age 25. Every 5 years till 65.

Management: Cone biopsy (microinvasive). Radical hysterectomy + lymphadenectomy (IA2-IIA). Chemoradiation (IIB-IVA).

## Ovarian Cancer

Screening: CA-125, Transvaginal USG. No effective population screening.

Most common epithelial: Serous carcinoma. BRCA1/2 mutation risk. Treatment: TAH + BSO + omentectomy + chemotherapy (carboplatin + paclitaxel).

posts.title: Obstetric Emergencies for UPSC CMS: APH, PPH, Eclampsia and Shoulder Dystocia
posts.description: Obstetric emergencies for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — APH, PPH, eclampsia, shoulder dystocia, cord prolapse, and the emergency management protocols.
posts.excerpt: Obstetric emergencies for UPSC CMS — APH, PPH, eclampsia, shoulder dystocia with emergency management, drug doses, and prevention strategies.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## APH (Antepartum Haemorrhage)

**Placenta previa:** Painless bleeding after 28 weeks. USG diagnosis. Treatment depends on type and fetal maturity.

**Abruptio placentae:** Painful bleeding, tender uterus, shock. Vaginal delivery usually preferred. Fetal distress common.

## PPH (Postpartum Haemorrhage)

4Ts: Tone (atonic uterus - most common), Trauma (lacerations), Tissue (retained placenta), Thrombin (coagulopathy).

Management: Uterine massage, Oxytocin 10 units IV, Misoprostol 800 mcg PR, Balloon tamponade (Bakri), Surgery.

## Eclampsia

Seizures in pre-eclampsia. MgSO4 loading 4g IV over 15 min, then 1-2g/hr maintenance. Monitor: reflexes, respiratory rate, urine output.

posts.title: Pharmacology CNS Drugs for UPSC CMS: Analgesics, Anaesthetics, Antidepressants and Antiepileptics
posts.description: Pharmacology CNS drugs for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — analgesics, local anaesthetics, general anaesthetics, antidepressants, antiepileptics, antipsychotics with mechanisms.
posts.excerpt: Pharmacology CNS drugs for UPSC CMS — analgesics, anaesthetics, antidepressants, antiepileptics, antipsychotics with mechanisms, doses, and adverse effects.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Analgesics

**NSAIDs:** Inhibit COX (1 and 2). Decrease prostaglandins. Side effects: GI bleed, renal impairment, bronchospasm (aspirin).

**Opioids:** Morphine, Pethidine, Fentanyl. Mechanism: Mu receptor agonism. Side effects: respiratory depression, constipation, dependence.

## Antidepressants

**SSRIs:** Fluoxetine, Sertraline. Inhibit serotonin reuptake. Side effects: GI upset, sexual dysfunction.

**TCAs:** Amitriptyline. Inhibit NE + 5-HT reuptake. Side effects: anticholinergic, cardiac (arrhythmia), sedation.

## Antiepileptics

Phenytoin (Na+ channel), Carbamazepine (Na+ channel), Valproate (multiple), Phenobarbital (GABA), Levetiracetam (SV2A).

posts.title: Pharmacology Cardiac Drugs for UPSC CMS: Mechanisms, Doses and Side Effects
posts.description: Pharmacology cardiac drugs for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — anti-anginal, anti-arrhythmic, anti-hypertensive, anti-heart failure drugs with mechanisms and side effects.
posts.excerpt: Pharmacology cardiac drugs for UPSC CMS — anti-anginal, anti-arrhythmic, anti-hypertensive, heart failure drugs with mechanisms, doses, and adverse effects.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Anti-Anginal Drugs

- **Nitrates:** NO -> cGMP -> vasodilation. Side effects: headache, hypotension, tolerance.
- **Beta-blockers:** Reduce HR and contractility. Propranolol, Metoprolol, Atenolol.
- **Calcium channel blockers:** Verapamil (cardio-selective), Diltiazem, Amlodipine.

## Anti-Arrhythmic (Vaughan-Williams)

**Class I (Na+ channel):** IA (quinidine - prolonged APD), IB (lignocaine - shortened APD), IC (flecainide - no APD change).
**Class II (Beta-blockers):** Propranolol, Esmolol.
**Class III (K+ channel):** Amiodarone (most effective, multi-channel), Sotalol.
**Class IV (Ca2+ channel):** Verapamil, Diltiazem.

## Heart Failure Drugs

ACE-I, ARNI, Beta-blockers, MRAs, SGLT2i, Diuretics.

posts.title: Infectious Disease for UPSC CMS: Typhoid, Malaria, Dengue, HIV and Emerging Infections
posts.description: Infectious diseases for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — typhoid, malaria, dengue, HIV, hepatitis, leptospirosis, emerging infections, and the clinical approach.
posts.excerpt: Infectious diseases for UPSC CMS — typhoid, malaria, dengue, HIV, hepatitis with clinical features, lab diagnosis, treatment and prevention.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Typhoid

S. typhi. Step-ladder fever, rose spots, intestinal ulcers (terminal ileum). Widal test (not reliable). Blood culture (gold standard). Treatment: Azithromycin, Cefixime, Ciprofloxacin.

## Malaria

P. falciparum: Most severe, cerebral malaria, blackwater fever. P. vivax: Relapsing, benign tertian. P. malariae: Quartan, nephrotic syndrome.

## Dengue

NS1 (day 1-5), IgM (day 5+), IgG (day 10+). Warning signs: abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, mucosal bleeding, lethargy. NS1 > antigen, rising hematocrit.

posts.title: Surgery Abdominal Conditions for UPSC CMS: Appendicitis, Hernia, Intestinal Obstruction and Peritonitis
posts.description: Surgery abdominal conditions for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — appendicitis, intestinal obstruction, peritonitis, abdominal tuberculosis, and the clinical signs that diagnose each.
posts.excerpt: Surgery abdominal conditions for UPSC CMS — appendicitis, intestinal obstruction, peritonitis, abdominal TB with clinical signs, investigations and management.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Appendicitis

McBurney point tenderness, Rovsing sign (LLQ pressure -> RLQ pain), Psoas sign (pain on extension), Obturator sign (pain on internal rotation).

Ward signs: Rovsing, Cope (psoas), Cope (obturator), Dunphy (pain on coughing).

## Intestinal Obstruction

Causes: Adhesions (most common), Hernias, Tumors, Volvulus, Intussusception.

Features: Colicky abdominal pain, distension, vomiting (bilious then feculent), absolute constipation.

## Peritonitis

Generalised: Rigid abdomen, absent bowel sounds, rebound tenderness. Causes: perforated viscus, gangrenous bowel.

posts.title: Systemic Diseases with Skin Manifestations for UPSC CMS: DM, SLE, Sarcoidosis and More
posts.description: Systemic diseases with skin manifestations for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — diabetes, SLE, sarcoidosis, dermatomyositis, and the skin signs that point to internal disease.
posts.excerpt: Systemic diseases with skin manifestations for UPSC CMS — diabetes, SLE, sarcoidosis, dermatomyositis, and the skin signs that point to internal disease.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Diabetes Skin Manifestations

Necrobiosis lipoidica (shin, yellow-brown plaques), Granuloma annulare, Diabetic dermopathy (brown spots on shins), Eruptive xanthomas (triglycerides >1000), Acanthosis nigricans (insulin resistance).

## SLE Skin Signs

Malar rash (butterfly, spares nasolabial fold), Discoid lesions (scarring), Photosensitivity, Oral ulcers, Alopecia, Vasculitic lesions.

## Sarcoidosis

Lupus pernio (violaceous nodules on nose/ears), Erythema nodosum (shins), Maculopapular rash. Non-caseating granulomas on biopsy.

## Dermatomyositis

Gottron papules (MCP/PIP joints), Heliotrope rash (eyelids), Shawl sign (shoulders), Mechanic hands.

posts.title: Medicine Poisoning and Toxicology for UPSC CMS: Organophosphates, Snake Bite and Common Poisons
posts.description: Medicine poisoning and toxicology for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — organophosphates, snake bite, CO poisoning, heavy metals, alcohol, and management with antidotes.
posts.excerpt: Medicine poisoning for UPSC CMS — organophosphates, snake bite, CO poisoning, heavy metals, with antidotes, clinical features, and management protocols.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Organophosphate Poisoning

Cholinergic excess. SLUDGE: Salivation, Lacrimation, Urination, Defecation, GI cramps, Emesis. Muscle fasciculations, miosis, bronchorrhea, bradycardia.

Treatment: Atropine (titrate to dry secretions) + PAM (oxime) + supportive care. Measure via PAM before giving.

## Snake Bite

**Viper (hemotoxic):** Local swelling, bleeding, coagulopathy, AKI. Treatment: ASV (anti-snake venom), wound care.

**Cobra/Krait (neurotoxic):** Ptosis, respiratory paralysis. Treatment: ASV, ventilatory support.

## Carbon Monoxide

Cherry-red skin, headache, confusion, COHb >10%. Treatment: 100% O2, Hyperbaric O2 if severe.

posts.title: CNS Medicine for UPSC CMS: Meningitis, Epilepsy, Parkinson and Demyelinating Diseases
posts.description: CNS medicine for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — epilepsy types and drugs, Parkinson disease, MS, GBS, myasthenia gravis, and the neurological examination findings.
posts.excerpt: CNS medicine for UPSC CMS — epilepsy, Parkinson, MS, GBS, myasthenia gravis, drug mechanisms, and the neuro signs tested in clinical vignettes.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Epilepsy

**Generalized:** Tonic-clonic, Absence (petit mal), Myoclonic, Atonic.
**Focal:** Simple partial, Complex partial, Focal to bilateral tonic-clonic.

Drugs: Carbamazepine/Valproate (first-line focal), Valproate (first-line generalized), Lamotrigine (women of childbearing age), Levetiracetam.

## Parkinson Disease

Triad: Tremor (resting), Rigidity (lead-pipe/cogwheel), Bradykinesia. Treatment: Levodopa + Carbidopa (gold standard).

## Multiple Sclerosis

Autoimmune demyelination. Dissemination in space + time. Oligoclonal bands in CSF. MRI: Dawson fingers. Relapses treated with steroids.

## Myasthenia Gravis

Anti-AChR antibodies. Fluctuating muscle weakness. Ptosis, diplopia. Edrophonium test. Treatment: Pyridostigmine, Steroids, Thymectomy.

posts.title: Respiratory Medicine for UPSC CMS: Asthma, COPD, ILD, Pneumonia and Pleural Effusion
posts.description: Respiratory medicine for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — asthma, COPD, ILD, pneumonia classification, pleural effusion, pneumothorax, and the investigation approach.
posts.excerpt: Respiratory medicine for UPSC CMS — asthma, COPD, ILD, pneumonia, pleural effusion, pneumothorax with investigations, severity scoring and management.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Asthma

Reversible airway obstruction. Triggers: allergens, exercise, cold, infection. Features: wheeze, dyspnea, cough, worse at night.

Treatment: SABA (salbutamol) reliever. ICS (fluticasone) preventer. LABA + ICS for moderate-severe. Omalizumab for severe allergic.

## COPD

Irreversible obstruction. FEV1/FVC <0.70. GOLD staging by FEV1 % predicted. ABCD assessment by symptoms + exacerbation history.

## Pleural Effusion

Transudate: CCF, cirrhosis, nephrotic. Exudate: Infection, malignancy, PE (Light criteria).

## Pneumothorax

Primary: Spontaneous in tall thin men. Secondary: underlying lung disease. Tension: emergency, needle decompression (2nd ICS midclavicular).

posts.title: Endocrinology for UPSC CMS: Thyroid, Adrenal, Pituitary and Diabetes Deep Dive
posts.description: Endocrinology for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — thyroid disorders, adrenal insufficiency, pituitary tumors, calcium metabolism, and the endocrine facts tested every year.
posts.excerpt: Endocrinology for UPSC CMS — hyper/hypothyroidism, Cushing vs Addison, acromegaly, hyperparathyroidism, and the investigation algorithms.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Thyroid Disorders

**Hyperthyroidism:** Graves (TSI +ve, diffuse goitre, ophthalmopathy), Toxic multinodular, Toxic adenoma. Treatment: Carbimazole, PTU (1st trimester), Radioiodine, Surgery.

**Hypothyroidism:** Hashimoto (Anti-TPO +ve), Post-radioiodine, Post-surgical. Treatment: Levothyroxine.

## Adrenal

**Addison:** Hyperpigmentation, hypotension, hyponatremia, hyperkalemia. Causes: Autoimmune (primary), Pituitary (secondary). Treatment: Hydrocortisone + Fludrocortisone.

**Cushing:** Centripetal obesity, moon face, buffalo hump, purple striae, hypertension. Causes: ACTH-dependent (pituitary, ectopic), ACTH-independent (adenoma).

## Pituitary

**Acromegaly:** GH-secreting adenoma. Large hands/feet, coarse features. IGF-1 elevated.

posts.title: Neurology Stroke for UPSC CMS: Types, FAST Recognition, tPA Window and Management
posts.description: Stroke for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — ischemic vs hemorrhagic types, FAST recognition, time windows, tPA eligibility, BP management, and secondary prevention.
posts.excerpt: Stroke for UPSC CMS — ischemic vs hemorrhagic, FAST recognition, tPA eligibility, BP targets, and secondary prevention strategies.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## FAST Recognition

**F**ace: Drooping on one side
**A**rm: Weakness/numbness in one arm
**S**peech: Slurred, confused
**T**ime: Call emergency immediately

## Ischemic Stroke

85% of strokes. Types: Atherothrombotic, Lacunar, Cardioembolic (AF). Treatment: tPA (0.9 mg/kg, max 90mg) if within 4.5 hours. Mechanical thrombectomy up to 24 hours for large vessel.

## Hemorrhagic Stroke

15%. BP control (target <140 mmHg), Neurosurgical consultation, lower ICP (mannitol, hyperventilation). Poor prognosis.

## Secondary Prevention

Antiplatelet: Aspirin (150-300mg daily), or Aspirin + Dypiridamole. Anticoagulant if AF (DOAC preferred over warfarin). Statin. BP control.

posts.title: Blood Physiology for UPSC CMS: RBC, WBC, Platelets, Coagulation and Blood Groups
posts.description: Blood physiology for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — RBC indices, WBC differential, platelet function, coagulation cascade, blood groups, and transfusion medicine.
posts.excerpt: Blood physiology for UPSC CMS — RBC indices, WBC differential, coagulation cascade, blood groups, and transfusion compatibility tables.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## RBC Indices

MCV (fL): 80-100. MCH (pg): 27-31. MCHC (%): 32-36.
- Microcytic: MCV <80 (IDA, thalassemia, anemia of chronic disease)
- Normocytic: MCV 80-100 (hemolysis, aplastic)
- Macrocytic: MCV >100 (B12, folate, alcohol, liver disease)

## Coagulation Cascade

**Intrinsic:** XII -> XI -> IX -> VIII -> X (measured by aPTT)
**Extrinsic:** VII -> X (measured by PT/INR)
**Common:** X -> V -> II (prothrombin) -> I (fibrinogen)

## Blood Groups

ABO: A (A antigen), B (B antigen), AB (both), O (neither). Rh: Positive (D antigen present), Negative (D absent). Universal donor: O-. Universal recipient: AB+.

posts.title: Doctor Burnout in Government Hospitals: Causes, Coping Strategies and Long-Term Solutions
posts.description: Doctor burnout in government hospitals for UPSC CMS aspirants — causes, statistics, coping strategies, workload management, and long-term solutions for government doctors.
posts.excerpt: Doctor burnout in government hospitals — causes, statistics, coping strategies, workload management, and realistic expectations for UPSC CMS aspirants.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Causes of Burnout

High patient load (100-200/day in PHCs), inadequate infrastructure, staff shortages, emotional burden, administrative pressure, long working hours (12-hour shifts).

## Statistics

Studies show 40-60% of government doctors experience burnout. Junior residents at highest risk. Female doctors report higher emotional exhaustion.

## Coping Strategies

1. Set boundaries: leave on time when possible
2. Peer support: debrief with colleagues
3. Professional development: continuing medical education
4. Physical health: exercise, sleep, nutrition
5. Mindfulness: brief meditation during breaks

## Long-Term Solutions

Better staffing ratios, reduced workload caps, mental health support programs, career progression pathways.

posts.title: Nephrology for UPSC CMS: AKI, CKD, Glomerulonephritis and RRT
posts.description: Nephrology for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — AKI causes and RIFLE criteria, CKD staging, glomerulonephritis types with biopsy findings, nephrotic syndrome, and RRT.
posts.excerpt: Nephrology for UPSC CMS — AKI vs CKD, glomerulonephritis classification, nephrotic syndrome, biopsy findings, and renal replacement therapy indications.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## AKI Causes (PINCH)

**Pre-renal:** Hypovolemia, decreased effective circulating volume. BUN:Cr >20:1.
**Intrinsic:** ATN ( muddy brown casts), AIN, GN. BUN:Cr ~10-15:1.
**Post-renal:** Obstruction (stones, BPH, tumor).

## CKD Staging

Based on eGFR: Stage 1 (>90, kidney damage), Stage 2 (60-89), Stage 3a (45-59), Stage 3b (30-44), Stage 4 (15-29), Stage 5 (<15, dialysis).

## Glomerulonephritis

**Minimal change:** Children, selective proteinuria, normal on LM, effacement on EM. Steroid responsive.

**FSGS:** Non-selective proteinuria, segmental sclerosis on LM. Steroid resistant.

**MPGN:** "Tram-track" on LM. Type II: dense deposits on EM.

posts.title: Haematology for UPSC CMS: Anaemia Types, Clotting Disorders and Haematological Malignancies
posts.description: Haematology for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — iron deficiency, megaloblastic, hemolytic anaemia, clotting disorders (haemophilia, vWD, DIC), leukaemia, lymphoma, myeloma.
posts.excerpt: Haematology for UPSC CMS — anaemia classification, haemolytic anaemia, clotting disorders, leukaemia, lymphoma, myeloma with peripheral blood and bone marrow findings.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Iron Deficiency Anaemia

Microcytic, hypochromic. Causes: blood loss (menorrhagia, GI bleed), poor diet, malabsorption. Treatment: oral iron (ferrous sulfate 200mg), IV iron if malabsorption.

## Megaloblastic Anaemia

B12 or folate deficiency. Macrocytic (MCV >100). B12: neurological signs (subacute combined degeneration). Folate: no neurological signs.

## Haemolytic Anaemia

**Intrinsic (membrane):** Hereditary spherocytosis, elliptocytosis. Osmotic fragility test.
**Intrinsic (enzyme):** G6PD deficiency. Bite cells, Heinz bodies.
**Extrinsic:** Autoimmune (Warm/Cold), Microangiopathic (TTP, HUS, DIC).

## Leukaemia

AML: Myeloblasts, Auer rods. ALL: L1/L2/L3 (Burkitt). CML: Philadelphia chromosome. CLL: smudge cells.

posts.title: Medicine Gastroenterology for UPSC CMS: Peptic Ulcer, IBD, Liver Disease and Pancreatitis
posts.description: Gastroenterology for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — peptic ulcer, IBD (Crohn vs UC), chronic liver disease, acute pancreatitis, and management algorithms.
posts.excerpt: Gastroenterology for UPSC CMS — peptic ulcer, IBD, liver disease, pancreatitis with investigations, scoring systems, and management protocols.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Peptic Ulcer Disease

H. pylori (70%), NSAIDs (20%). Complications: bleeding (hematemesis, melena), perforation (rigid abdomen, free air), obstruction (pyloric stenosis).

Treatment: PPI + dual antibiotics (amoxicillin + clarithromycin or metronidazole) for 14 days.

## IBD

**Ulcerative colitis:** Continuous from rectum. Pseudopolyps. Toxic megacolon. Treatment: 5-ASA, steroids, azathioprine, biologics.

**Crohn:** Skip lesions. Transmural. Fistulas, strictures. Any GI tract. Perianal disease.

## Acute Pancreatitis

Causes: Gallstones (40%), Alcohol (30%). Scoring: APACHE II, BISAP, Ranson. CT severity index.

posts.title: Rheumatology for UPSC CMS: RA, SLE, Vasculitis and the Autoantibody Panel Explained
posts.description: Rheumatology for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — RA, SLE, vasculitis (ANCA, PAN), spondyloarthropathy, autoantibodies (ANA, RF, Anti-CCP, Anti-dsDNA), and management.
posts.excerpt: Rheumatology for UPSC CMS — RA, SLE, vasculitis, autoantibody interpretation, classification criteria, and DMARD management algorithms.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Rheumatoid Arthritis

Symmetrical small joint polyarthritis. Morning stiffness >1 hour. RF (70%) + Anti-CCP (specific). Extra-articular: nodules, pulmonary fibrosis, vasculitis, amyloidosis.

Treatment: Methotrexate (first-line DMARD) + Sulfasalazine + Hydroxychloroquine (triple therapy). Add steroids for flare. Biologics (TNF-alpha inhibitors) for refractory.

## SLE

Malar rash, photosensitivity, oral ulcers, arthritis, serositis, renal (nephrotic syndrome), neuro (seizures, psychosis), hematological.

ANA (sensitive, not specific), Anti-dsDNA (specific, correlates with disease activity), Anti-Sm (specific).

## Vasculitis

**PAN:** Polyarteritis nodosa. Medium vessel. HBV associated. No pulmonary involvement.
**GPA (Wegener):** c-ANCA (PR3). Upper airway, lung, kidney.
**MPA:** p-ANCA (MPO). Pulmonary-renal syndrome.

posts.title: CNS Infections for UPSC CMS: Meningitis, Encephalitis and Brain Abscess
posts.description: CNS infections for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — meningitis (bacterial, TB, viral), encephalitis (JEV, HSV), brain abscess, and the CSF findings that diagnose each.
posts.excerpt: CNS infections for UPSC CMS — bacterial meningitis, TB meningitis, encephalitis, brain abscess with CSF findings, treatment and prognosis.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Bacterial Meningitis

Organisms: S. pneumoniae (adults), N. meningitidis (children/young adults), H. influenzae (post-Hib vaccine: rare).

CSF: Turbid, WBC >1000 (neutrophils), protein high, glucose low (<40), Gram stain.

Treatment: Dexamethasone + Ceftriaxone + Vancomycin. Ampicillin if Listeria risk (elderly, immunocompromised, pregnancy).

## TB Meningitis

CSF: Clear/fibrinous, WBC 50-500 (lymphocytic), protein high, glucose very low. Long track signs, basal exudates on imaging.

Treatment: HRZE (isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide, ethambutol) + steroids.

## Viral Encephalitis

HSV-1: Temporal lobe involvement on MRI. Treatment: Acyclovir IV. JEV: Japanese encephalitis, rice fields, pigs.

posts.title: Valvular Heart Disease for UPSC CMS: Murmurs, Severity Grading and Surgical Indications
posts.description: Valvular heart disease for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — murmur characteristics, severity grading, echocardiography findings, and surgical indications for each valve.
posts.excerpt: Valvular heart disease for UPSC CMS — murmur descriptions, severity grading, echo findings, and surgical thresholds for mitral, aortic, tricuspid, and pulmonary valves.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Mitral Stenosis

Opening snap after A2. Diastolic rumble, apex, left lateral decubitus, presystolic accentuation. Causes: rheumatic (90%). Complications: AF, LA thrombus, pulmonary hypertension, right heart failure.

## Mitral Regurgitation

Pan-systolic murmur, apex, radiates to axilla. Causes: MVP, papillary muscle rupture (post-MI), rheumatic, flail leaflet.

## Aortic Stenosis

Ejection systolic murmur, right 2nd ICS, radiates to carotids. Crescendo-decrescendo. Soft S2. Causes: calcific (elderly), rheumatic, bicuspid valve. Symptoms: angina, syncope, dyspnea.

## Aortic Regurgitation

Early diastolic, high-pitched, decrescendo. Left sternal edge. Causes: aortic root dilation (Marfan), infective endocarditis, rheumatic.

posts.title: Heart Failure for UPSC CMS: NYHA Classification, Management and the 2022 ESC Guidelines
posts.description: Heart failure for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — NYHA classification, pathophysiology, management (ACE-I, ARNI, beta-blocker, MRA, SGLT2i), and acute vs chronic distinction.
posts.excerpt: Heart failure for UPSC CMS — NYHA classification, pathophysiology, quadruple therapy, acute management, and the 2022 ESC guideline changes.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## NYHA Classification

**Class I:** No limitation. Ordinary activity causes no symptoms.
**Class II:** Slight limitation. Comfortable at rest, ordinary activity causes fatigue.
**Class III:** Marked limitation. Less than ordinary activity causes symptoms.
**Class IV:** Unable to carry out any activity without discomfort. Symptoms at rest.

## HFrEF Management (2022 ESC)

Four pillars:
1. **ARNI** (sacubitril/valsartan) or ACE-I/ARB
2. **Beta-blocker** (bisoprolol, carvedilol, metoprolol succinate)
3. **MRA** (spironolactone, eplerenone)
4. **SGLT2 inhibitor** (dapagliflozin, empagliflozin)

Add: Diuretics (symptom relief), Ivabradine (if HR >70 on max beta-blocker).

posts.title: Medicine Arrhythmias for UPSC CMS: ECG Recognition and Emergency Management
posts.description: Cardiac arrhythmias for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — ECG recognition of AF, AFlutter, VT, VF, heart block, WPW, and emergency management algorithms.
posts.excerpt: Cardiac arrhythmias for UPSC CMS — ECG recognition of AF, VT, VF, heart blocks, WPW, and ACLS algorithms for management.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Atrial Fibrillation

Irregularly irregular. No P waves. Variable R-R intervals. CHA2DS2-VASc score for anticoagulation: C=1, H=1, A2=2, D=1, S2=2, V=1, A=1, Sc=1. Score >=2 = anticoagulate.

## Atrial Flutter

Sawtooth F waves. Usually 2:1 block (300 atrial rate, 150 ventricular). Treat rate (beta-blocker, diltiazem), rhythm (amiodarone), anticoagulate.

## Ventricular Tachycardia

Wide QRS (>0.12s), regular. Hemodynamically unstable = immediate synchronized cardioversion. Stable = amiodarone IV.

## Ventricular Fibrillation

Chaotic, no organized QRS. Immediate defibrillation + CPR + epinephrine + amiodarone.

## Heart Blocks

1st degree: PR >0.20s. 2nd degree Type I (Wenckebach): progressive PR prolongation. 2nd degree Type II (Mobitz): sudden dropped beats. 3rd degree: complete dissociation, atrial and ventricular rates independent.

posts.title: Dermatology Drug Eruptions and Leprosy for UPSC CMS: Patterns, Types and Clinical Recognition
posts.description: Dermatology drug eruptions and leprosy for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — drug reaction patterns, fixed drug eruption, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and leprosy classification.
posts.excerpt: Dermatology drug eruptions and leprosy for UPSC CMS — reaction patterns, SJS/TEN, fixed drug eruption, leprosy classification, and the skin findings tested.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Drug Eruptions

**Morbilliform:** Most common. Symmetric maculopapular rash. Starts on trunk, spreads.

**Fixed drug eruption:** Round erythematous plaque, recurs at same site. Lips, genitalia common. Darker pigmentation after healing.

**Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS):** Targetoid lesions, mucous membrane involvement, fever. <10% BSA involved. Mortality 1-5%.

**Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN):** >30% BSA detachment. Mucosal involvement. Mortality 30-50%.

## Leprosy

**Classification (Ridley-Jopling):**
- TT (Tuberculoid): 1-2 hypopigmented macules, strong +ve Lepromin
- BT (Borderline tuberculoid): 3-10 lesions
- BB (Mid-borderline): Variable
- BL (Borderline lepromatous): Many lesions, +ve Lepromin
- LL (Lepromatous): Diffuse, leonine facies, -ve Lepromin

posts.description: Communication skills for UPSC CMS — breaking bad news (SPIKES), informed consent, patient counseling, and the communication scenarios tested in practical exams.

posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## S PIKES Protocol

**S**etting: Private, comfortable, no interruptions.
**P**erception: Ask what they understand.
**I**nvitation: Ask if they want details.
**K**nowledge: Share information in small chunks.
**E**motions: Acknowledge and respond to feelings.
**S**trategy: Discuss next steps.

## Informed Consent

Elements: Disclosure, Understanding, Voluntariness, Competence, Consent. Written consent for surgery, anesthesia, research. Emergency exception: no consent needed to save life.

## Counseling Skills

Active listening, empathy, non-judgmental. Motivational interviewing for behavior change (smoking, diet).

posts.title: GI Endoscopy for UPSC CMS Aspirants: OGD, Colonoscopy and the Findings You Must Recognize
posts.description: GI endoscopy for UPSC CMS — OGD and colonoscopy findings, common endoscopic appearances (ulcers, varices, polyps, cancers), and the endoscopic signs tested in exams.
posts.excerpt: GI endoscopy for UPSC CMS — OGD and colonoscopy findings, common appearances, and the endoscopic signs tested as image-based questions.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## OGD Findings

**Gastritis:** Redness, erosions, mucosal friability.
**Peptic ulcer:** Benign (smooth edges, radiating folds) vs Malignant (heaped-up edges, irregular folds).
**Duodenal ulcer:** Anterior wall duodenal bulb (most common).
**Barrett esophagus:** Salmon-colored columnar epithelium above Z-line.

**Ulcerative colitis:** Continuous from rectum. Pseudopolyps, loss of vascular pattern.
**Crohn:** Skip lesions, cobblestone mucosa, strictures.

Used for biliary and pancreatic duct imaging. ERCP is therapeutic too (stone extraction, stenting).

posts.title: Orthopaedics Spine Injuries for UPSC CMS: Classification, Management and Complications
posts.description: Orthopaedics spine injuries for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — cervical, thoracic, lumbar spine fracture classification (Denis, AO), neurological assessment, and management.
posts.excerpt: Spine injuries for UPSC CMS — cervical, thoracic, lumbar fracture classification, neurological assessment, and management principles.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Cervical Spine

**Jefferson fracture (C1):** Burst fracture from axial loading. 4-part burst on X-ray.

**Hangman fracture (C2):** Bilateral pars fractures. From hyperextension.

**Odontoid fracture (C2):** Type I (tip), Type II (base — most common, unstable), Type III (extends into body).

**Clay-shoveler:** Spinous process fracture of C7/T1/T2.

## Thoracic/Lumbar

**Denis 3-column:**
- Anterior: Anterior 2/3 vertebral body + anterior longitudinal ligament
- Middle: Posterior 1/3 vertebral body + posterior longitudinal ligament
- Posterior: Pedicles, laminae, spinous processes + ligamentum flavum

Compression: Anterior column only. Burst: Anterior + Middle. Flexion-distraction: All three.

posts.title: ENT Hearing Loss Classification for UPSC CMS: Conductive, Sensorineural and Mixed Compared
posts.description: ENT hearing loss classification for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — conductive vs sensorineural, causes, investigations (Weber, Rinne, Audiometry), and management.
posts.excerpt: ENT hearing loss classification for UPSC CMS — conductive, sensorineural and mixed compared with causes, investigations, and management.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Classification

**Conductive:** Problem in outer/middle ear. Sound cannot reach cochlea. Causes: wax, perforation, otosclerosis, otitis media.

**Sensorineural:** Problem in inner ear or 8th nerve. Causes: presbycusis, noise trauma, Menieres, acoustic neuroma, drugs (gentamicin).

**Mixed:** Both conductive and sensorineural components.

## Investigations

**Weber test:** Tuning fork on forehead. Lateralizes to affected ear in conductive, to normal ear in sensorineural.

**Rinne test:** Tuning fork on mastoid then near ear. Air conduction > Bone conduction = Rinne positive (normal or SNHL). BC > AC = Rinne negative (conductive).

## Management

Conductive: treat cause, surgery if needed. Sensorineural: hearing aids, cochlear implants.

posts.title: Ophthalmology Glaucoma for UPSC CMS: Types, IOP, Visual Fields and Treatment Algorithms
posts.description: Ophthalmology glaucoma for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — types of glaucoma, intraocular pressure, visual field defects, optic disc changes, and stepwise treatment.
posts.excerpt: Glaucoma for UPSC CMS — types, IOP, visual field defects, optic disc cupping, and the stepwise treatment algorithm tested every year.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Types of Glaucoma

**Primary open-angle:** Most common. Insidious. Cupped optic disc, field defects (arcuate, nasal step). IOP elevated. Treatment: eye drops -> laser -> surgery.

**Primary angle-closure:** Acute (halos, severe pain, fixed mid-dilated pupil, nausea). Treatment: pilocarpine, acetazolamide, peripheral iridotomy.

**Secondary:** Due to other conditions (uveitis, steroid use, trauma, neovascular).

## Visual Field Defects

- **Arcuate scotoma:** Arc-shaped defect from disc to macula
- **Nasal step:** Step defect respecting horizontal midline
- **Paracentral scotoma:** Small defect near fixation
- **Tubular vision:** End-stage glaucoma

## Treatment Algorithm

First line: Prostaglandin analogs (latanoprost). Second: Beta-blockers (timolol). Third: CA inhibitors (dorzolamide). Add pilocarpine for angle-closure.

posts.title: Urology High-Yield for UPSC CMS: Common Urological Conditions and Their Management
posts.description: Urology high-yield topics for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — renal calculi, UTIs, BPH, bladder cancer, prostate cancer, and the investigations and management tested.
posts.excerpt: Urology high-yield for UPSC CMS — renal calculi, UTIs, BPH, bladder and prostate cancer, investigations, and management protocols.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Renal Calculi

**Calcium oxalate (80%):** Envelopes/dumbbell on X-ray. Risk factors: hypercalciuria, hyperoxaluria, low citrate.

**Struvite (triple phosphate):** Staghorn. Associated with Proteus infection.

**Uric acid:** Radiolucent. Associated with gout, acidic urine.

Management: Conservative (<5mm, 80% pass spontaneously), ESWL (5-10mm), PCNL (>10mm or staghorn).

## BPH

Enlargement of transitional zone. Symptoms: hesitancy, weak stream, nocturia, incomplete emptying. Treatment: Alpha-blockers (tamsulosin), 5-alpha-reductase inhibitors (finasteride), TURP.

## Bladder Cancer

Most common: Transitional cell carcinoma. Risk: smoking, occupational (aniline dyes). Presents with painless hematuria.

posts.title: Surgical Oncology for UPSC CMS: Common Cancers, Staging and Surgical Management
posts.description: Surgical oncology for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — common cancers (oesophagus, stomach, colon, liver, pancreas), TNM staging, surgical options, and adjuvant therapy.
posts.excerpt: Surgical oncology for UPSC CMS — common cancers, TNM staging, surgical management, and the AJCC staging facts tested in exams.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Oesophageal Cancer

Squamous cell carcinoma (upper/mid), Adenocarcinoma (lower, Barrett). Treatment: Ivor-Lewis oesophagectomy for resectable disease.

## Gastric Cancer

Most common in antrum (India). Laen Classification: Type I (expansile), Type II (ulcerative), Type III (infiltrative). Treatment: D2 gastrectomy + adjuvant chemo.

## Colorectal Cancer

Right colon: Ann Arbor configuration (exophytic). Left colon: Constricting (apple-core on barium). Treatment: Segmental colectomy + lymphadenectomy.

## TNM Staging

T (tumor extent), N (nodal), M (metastasis). Stage grouping determines treatment.

posts.title: CNS Physiology for UPSC CMS: EEG, Sleep, Motor Control and Reflexes Explained
posts.description: CNS physiology for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — EEG wave patterns, sleep stages, motor control (UMN vs LMN), reflex arcs, and autonomic control.
posts.excerpt: CNS physiology for UPSC CMS — EEG patterns, sleep stages, UMN vs LMN signs, reflex arcs, and autonomic nervous system control.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## EEG Waves

**Alpha (8-13 Hz):** Awake, eyes closed, relaxed. Centroparietal.
**Beta (14-30 Hz):** Active thinking, anxiety. Frontocentral.
**Theta (4-7 Hz):** Drowsiness, children. Temporal.
**Delta (0.5-3 Hz):** Deep sleep, coma. Frontal in adults, normal in children.

## Sleep Stages

NREM: Stage 1 (drowsy), Stage 2 (sleep spindles), Stage 3/4 (delta sleep = deep). REM: Rapid eye movement, dreaming, brain active, body paralyzed.

## UMN vs LMN Signs

| Feature | UMN | LMN |
|---------|-----|-----|
| Tone | Increased | Decreased |
| Reflexes | Increased | Decreased |
| Atrophy | Minimal | Marked |
| Fasciculations | Absent | Present |
| Babinski | Present | Absent |

posts.title: Respiratory Physiology for UPSC CMS: Lung Volumes, Compliance and Gas Exchange
posts.description: Respiratory physiology for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — lung volumes and capacities, compliance, airway resistance, gas exchange, oxygen dissociation curve, and regulation.
posts.excerpt: Respiratory physiology for UPSC CMS — lung volumes, compliance, V/Q matching, oxygen dissociation curve, alveolar ventilation and the key equations.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Lung Volumes

Tidal volume (TV): 500 mL. Inspiratory reserve volume (IRV): 3000 mL. Expiratory reserve volume (ERV): 1200 mL. Residual volume (RV): 1200 mL.

Lung capacities: VC = TV + IRV + ERV = 4600. FRC = ERV + RV = 2400.

## Compliance

= Change in volume / Change in pressure. Normal: 200 mL/cmH2O.
Emphysema: compliance increased (floppy lungs).
Fibrosis: compliance decreased (stiff lungs).

## O2 Dissociation Curve

Right shift: increased PCO2, increased H+, increased temperature, increased 2,3-DPG. Left shift: opposite.

posts.title: Cardiac Physiology for UPSC CMS: Cardiac Cycle, ECG, Heart Sounds and Hemodynamics
posts.description: Cardiac physiology for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — cardiac cycle phases, ECG waves, heart sounds, pressure changes, Frank-Starling mechanism, and cardiac output.
posts.excerpt: Cardiac physiology for UPSC CMS — cardiac cycle phases, ECG interpretation, heart sounds, Frank-Starling, cardiac output equations and hemodynamics.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Cardiac Cycle

**Atrial systole:** Atria contract, push remaining blood into ventricles (80% already filled passively). "A" wave.

**Isovolumetric contraction:** AV valves close, ventricles contract. S1 produced. Pressure rises to aortic pressure.

**Rapid ejection:** Aortic valve opens. Blood ejected rapidly.
**Reduced ejection:** Ejection continues slowly.

**Isovolumetric relaxation:** Aortic valve closes, S2 produced. Pressure falls.

**Rapid filling:** AV valves open, blood rushes in.
**Diastasis:** Slow filling phase.

## ECG Waves

P wave = atrial depolarization. PR interval = AV conduction. QRS = ventricular depolarization. ST segment = ventricular plateau. T wave = ventricular repolarization.

## Frank-Starling Mechanism

Increased preload -> increased stretch -> increased force of contraction. Explains how heart adjusts output to venous return.

posts.title: Renal Physiology for UPSC CMS: GFR, RAAS, Acid-Base and the Equations Every Candidate Must Know
posts.description: Renal physiology for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — GFR, RAAS, concentrating mechanisms, acid-base handling, and the equations tested every year.
posts.excerpt: Renal physiology for UPSC CMS — GFR, RAAS, concentrating mechanisms, acid-base handling, and the exact equations tested every year.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## GFR

Normal: 125 mL/min. Measured by inulin clearance (gold standard). Estimated by creatinine clearance or eGFR (CKD-EPI formula).

Creatinine clearance > GFR because of tubular secretion.

## RAAS

Renin (JG cells) -> Angiotensinogen -> Angiotensin I -> ACE (lung) -> Angiotensin II -> Aldosterone (zona glomerulosa).

Effects: Vasoconstriction (angiotensin II), Na+ retention + K+ excretion (aldosterone), Thirst + ADH (angiotensin II).

## Concentrating Mechanism

Countercurrent multiplier (Loop of Henle) + Countercurrent exchanger (vasa recta). ADH increases water reabsorption in collecting duct.

posts.title: Gynaecology Common Disorders for UPSC CMS: PCOS, Fibroids, Endometriosis and PID
posts.description: Gynaecology common disorders for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — PCOS, uterine fibroids, endometriosis, PID, their diagnosis, investigations, and management.
posts.excerpt: Gynaecology common disorders for UPSC CMS — PCOS, fibroids, endometriosis, PID, and the management decisions tested in every year's paper.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## PCOS

Polycystic ovary syndrome. Rotterdam criteria: 2 of 3 — Oligo/anovulation, Hyperandrogenism (clinical/biochemical), Polycystic ovaries on USG.

Management: Lifestyle (first-line), Metformin, OCPs (for cycle regulation), Clomiphene for infertility, Spironolactone for hirsutism.

## Uterine Fibroids (Leiomyoma)

Benign smooth muscle tumor. Types: Intramural, Submucosal, Subserosal, Cervical.

Symptoms: Menorrhagia, dysmenorrhoea, pelvic mass, infertility.
Treatment: Myomectomy (desire fertility), Hysterectomy (completed family), Uterine artery embolization, MRI-guided FUS.

## Endometriosis

Ectopic endometrial tissue. Common sites: Ovaries (chocolate cyst), Pouch of Douglas, Uterosacral ligaments.

Diagnosis: Laparoscopy (gold standard). Treatment: NSAIDs, OCPs, Progestins, GnRH analogues, Surgery.

posts.description: Labour and delivery management for UPSC CMS — stages of labour, normal delivery steps, partograph use, assisted delivery (forceps, vacuum), and complications.
posts.excerpt: Labour and delivery management for UPSC CMS — stages of labour, partograph, assisted delivery indications, and complication recognition.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Stages of Labour

**First stage:** Cervical dilatation (0-10cm). Latent phase (0-3cm, slow), Active phase (3-10cm, 1cm/hr). Duration: 8-12 hrs (primigravida), 5-8 hrs (multigravida).

**Second stage:** Full dilatation to delivery of baby. Duration: 1-2 hrs (primi), 30 min (multi).

**Third stage:** Delivery of baby to delivery of placenta. Active management: Oxytocin + controlled cord traction.

## Partograph

Records: Cervical dilatation (alert line at 4cm, action at 1cm/hr less), FHR, membranes, liquor, contractions, pulse, BP.

## Complications

Prolonged labour, obstructed labour, cord prolapse, shoulder dystocia, PPH (4Ts: Tone, Trauma, Tissue, Thrombin).

posts.title: Surgery Hernia Types for UPSC CMS: Inguinal, Femoral, Umbilical and Incisional Compared
posts.description: Surgery hernia types for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — inguinal (indirect/direct), femoral, umbilical, incisional hernias with classification, complications and management.
posts.excerpt: Hernia types for UPSC CMS — inguinal indirect/direct, femoral, umbilical, incisional hernias with classification, complications, and the McBurney point trick.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Inguinal Hernia

**Indirect:** Protrudes through deep inguinal ring, lateral to inferior epigastric vessels. Follows inguinal canal. Covers entire canal. Congenital (patent processus vaginalis).

**Direct:** Protrudes through Hesselbach triangle (medial to IEV). Does not cover full canal. Acquired (weak abdominal wall).

## Femoral Hernia

Protrudes through femoral canal. Below inguinal ligament. More common in women. HIGH risk of strangulation.

## Umbilical Hernia

Through umbilical ring. Common in infants (often closes by age 2). In adults: associated with obesity, multiparity, ascites.

## Incisional Hernia

At previous surgical scar. Risk factors: obesity, wound infection, poor suturing.

posts.title: Surgery Thyroid Diseases for UPSC CMS: Goitre, Thyroiditis and Thyroid Cancer Classification
posts.description: Surgery thyroid diseases for UPSC CMS — goitre types, thyroiditis, thyroid carcinoma (papillary, follicular, medullary, anaplastic), and management.
posts.excerpt: Thyroid diseases for UPSC CMS — goitre, thyroiditis, thyroid cancer types, Bethesda classification, and the management decisions tested in exams.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Goitre Classification

**Diffuse:** Entire gland enlarged. Graves disease (hyperthyroid), Hashimoto (hypothyroid).
**Multinodular:** Multiple nodules. Most common thyroid disease.
**Solitary nodule:** Single nodule. 10-20% malignant risk.

## Thyroiditis

- **Hashimoto:** Anti-TPO, Anti-thyroglobulin. Painless goitre -> hypothyroidism.
- **De Quervain:** Painful goitre, elevated ESR. Usually post-viral. Self-limiting.
- **Subacute (silent):** Painless, post-partum. May cause transient hyper -> hypo -> recovery.

## Thyroid Cancer Types

**Papillary (80%):** Slow-growing, lymph node spread. Treatment: total thyroidectomy + radioiodine.
**Follicular (10%):** Hematogenous spread (bone, lung). Need total thyroidectomy.
**Medullary:** Calcitonin elevated. RET mutation (MEN2). Prophylactic thyroidectomy if RET+.
**Anaplastic (1%):** Very aggressive, elderly. Poor prognosis.

posts.title: Surgery Breast Diseases for UPSC CMS: Benign vs Malignant, TNM Staging and Management
posts.description: Surgery breast diseases for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — benign lumps, carcinoma breast, TNM staging, treatment algorithms, and the clinical signs tested in exams.
posts.excerpt: Breast diseases for UPSC CMS — benign lumps vs carcinoma breast, TNM staging, treatment algorithms, and the clinical signs that appear as image questions.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Benign Breast Diseases

**Fibroadenoma:** Young women (15-35), mobile, well-defined lump. Treatment: excision.

**Fibrocystic change:** Pre-menopausal women, cyclical pain, lumpy breasts.

**Galactocele:** Milk-filled cyst in lactating women.

## Carcinoma Breast

**Risk factors:** Female, age >50, family history (BRCA1/2), early menarche, late menopause, nulliparity, HRT.

**Clinical features:** Hard, irregular, fixed lump. Skin changes (peau dorange), nipple retraction, axillary nodes.

**TNM Staging:** T (tumor size), N (nodal involvement), M (metastasis). Stages I-IV.

## Treatment

Stage I-II: Surgery (BCT or MRM) + Adjuvant therapy.
Stage III: Neoadjuvant chemo -> Surgery -> Adjuvant.
Stage IV: Palliative.

Two components: PMJAY (insurance, Rs 5 lakh/family/year) and HWCs (health and wellness centres, 1.5 lakh targeted).

Population-based screening for diabetes, hypertension, and common cancers (breast, cervical, oral).

posts.title: Contraception Methods for UPSC CMS: Effectiveness, Mechanism and Failure Rates Compared
posts.description: Contraception methods for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — all methods compared by effectiveness, mechanism of action, failure rates, advantages and contraindications.

posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Barrier Methods

Male condom (98% effective with perfect use), Female condom, Diaphragm, Cervical cap.

## Hormonal Methods

**Combined oral contraceptive pill:** Contains estrogen + progestogen. Mechanism: suppress ovulation, thicken cervical mucus. Pearl index: 0.3.

**Progestogen-only pill:** Suppress ovulation, thicken mucus. Pearl index: 0.5.

**Injectables:** Depot medroxyprogesterone acetate (DMPA). 3-monthly injection.

Copper IUCD: Non-hormonal. Effective 5 years. Levonorgestrel IUCD (Mirena): Hormonal, reduces bleeding.

## Permanent Methods

Male sterilization (vasectomy), Female sterilization (tubal ligation).

## Natural Methods

Calendar method, Basal body temperature, Cervical mucus (Billings).

**First trimester (before 14 weeks):** First visit as soon as pregnancy confirmed. Folic acid 400mcg, dating scan, blood group, Hb, urine, VDRL, HIV, HBsAg.

**Second trimester (14-28 weeks):** Visit at 16 weeks, 20 weeks (anomaly scan), 24 weeks (glucose tolerance).

posts.title: Surgical Anastomosis Types: End-to-End, End-to-Side and When to Use Each (UPSC CMS)
posts.description: Surgical anastomosis types for UPSC CMS — end-to-end, end-to-side, side-to-side, stapling vs hand-sewn, complications, and the anastomosis facts tested in exams.
posts.excerpt: Surgical anastomosis types for UPSC CMS — end-to-end, end-to-side, side-to-side, stapling vs hand-sewn, complications and exam-relevant facts.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Types of Anastomosis

**End-to-end:** Both ends joined directly. Used when bowel diameter is equal (ileum-ileum, colo-colic).

**End-to-side:** End of one to side of another. Used in biliary-enteric, gastrojejunostomy.

**Side-to-side:** Both sides joined. Used in enteroenterostomy, jejunojejunostomy.

## Stapling vs Hand-Sewn

Stapling: Faster, more consistent, less tissue handling. Hand-sewn: More versatile, cheaper. Staplers preferred for ileal pouch-anal anastomosis.

## Complications

Stricture, leak (most dangerous — peritonitis, abscess, fistula), bleeding, wound infection.

posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team
posts.body:
## Suture Materials

**Absorbable:** Catgut (plain/chromic), Polyglycolic acid (Vicryl), Polydioxanone (PDS). Used for internal tissues.

**Non-absorbable:** Silk, Nylon (Ethilon), Prolene (polypropylene), Stainless steel. Used for skin, vascular anastomosis.

## Needle Types

- **Cutting needle**: Triangular cross-section, for tough tissue (skin)
- **Round body (taper)**: Round cross-section, for soft tissue (intestine)
- **Reverse cutting**: Outer curve cutting, for tough tissue

## Suture Patterns

**Interrupted:** Individual knots. Advantage: if one fails, others hold.
**Continuous (running):** One long suture. Advantage: even tension distribution.
**Mattress:** Vertical (everting) or Horizontal (apposing).

posts.title: Spaced Repetition Flashcards for UPSC CMS: How to Build a Deck That Cuts Revision Time by 60%
posts.description: How to build and use spaced repetition flashcards for UPSC CMS and NEET PG — the SM-2 algorithm, card design principles, and the exact subjects to prioritize.

posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team

faqs.q: How many flashcards should I make for UPSC CMS?
faqs.a: Start with 500-800 cards covering the highest-yield topics. Focus on: one-liners, drug classifications, clinical signs, and PYQ facts. Quality > quantity — better to master 500 cards than to have 5000 mediocre ones.

faqs.q: Should I use Anki or physical flashcards?
faqs.a: Anki (free, desktop + mobile) is better for large decks because it automates spaced repetition. Physical cards are better for visual topics (anatomy diagrams, histology). Use both for best results.

faqs.q: What makes a good flashcard?
faqs.a: One question, one answer. Maximum 15 words. Use cloze deletion (fill-in-the-blank) for facts. Use images for visual topics. Avoid long paragraphs.

posts.body:
## The SM-2 Algorithm

SM-2 (used by Anki): After answering, rate difficulty (Again/Hard/Good/Easy). Card reappears based on ease factor:
- Again: < 1 minute
- Hard: 1-3 days
- Good: 3-7 days (default)
- Easy: 10+ days

## Card Design Principles

- One question, one answer
- Max 15 words per card
- Cloze deletion for facts
- Images for visual topics
- NO long paragraphs

## Subject Priority

Highest ROI: PSM (many facts), Pharmacology (drug facts), Microbiology (organisms), FSM (straight facts).
Lower ROI: Medicine (complex concepts), Surgery (procedures).

## Daily Flashcard Routine

Morning: 20 min review of due cards
Evening: 10 min add new cards from today's study
Weekly: 30 min cleanup (edit/delete stale cards)

posts.title: Reading Comprehension for Long UPSC CMS Stems: Speed-Reading Techniques for Medical Text
posts.description: Speed-reading techniques for long UPSC CMS clinical vignettes — how to extract the key information from long stems without missing critical details.
posts.excerpt: Speed-reading techniques for long UPSC CMS clinical vignettes — extract key information fast without missing critical details that determine the right answer.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team

faqs.q: Why are UPSC CMS stems so long?
faqs.a: Long clinical vignettes test integrated knowledge — the ability to connect history, examination findings, and investigations to arrive at a diagnosis and management plan. This is what makes CMS and NEET PG different from simpler exams.

faqs.q: How fast should I read a typical CMS stem?
faqs.a: Target 40-50 seconds for a typical 100-150 word stem. Practice by timing yourself and gradually reducing reading time without missing key details.

faqs.q: What parts of the stem are most important?
faqs.a: Demographics (age, sex, occupation), chief complaint, duration, key examination findings, and the investigation results. These contain 80% of the information needed to answer.

posts.body:
## The Skim-Scan Technique

1. Read the first sentence (demographics + chief complaint)
2. Scan for numbers, lab values, and investigation results
3. Read the last sentence (what is being asked)
4. Return to fill in the middle only if needed

This reduces average reading time by 40%.

## Identifying Key Information

**Critical:** Age, sex, duration, key complaint, abnormal exam finding, abnormal lab result.
**Ignorable:** Patient occupation unless relevant, negative review of systems, normal lab values.

## Avoiding Red Herrings

Exam setters include plausible but irrelevant information. Key rule: if the information does not narrow your differential diagnosis, it is a red herring.

## Practice Method

Practice 20 long stems daily, timing yourself. Start at 60 seconds per stem, work down to 40 seconds. Use our question bank for unlimited practice.

posts.title: 50 Commonly Confused Topics in UPSC CMS: The Pairs That Always Appear as Options
posts.description: 50 commonly confused topic pairs in UPSC CMS — the distractors that appear together as options, how to tell them apart, and the mnemonics that stick.
posts.excerpt: 50 commonly confused topic pairs in UPSC CMS — the distractors that always appear together as options. Learn the exact differences that separate right from wrong.
posts.author: CrackCMS Editorial Team

faqs.q: Why do confused topics appear in pairs?
faqs.a: Exam setters deliberately place similar-sounding conditions or drugs together to test depth of knowledge. This is the most common exam technique across all medical PG exams.

faqs.q: How do I tell similar conditions apart?
faqs.a: Focus on the ONE key differentiating feature. Examples: MI vs pericarditis (ST elevation: convex vs concave, PR depression), SLE vs RA (ANA pattern, joint involvement pattern).

faqs.q: Are these topic pairs the same for NEET PG?
faqs.a: Yes — 70-80% of these pairs are identical for NEET PG. The distinguishing features are the same. Learning these pairs helps both exams simultaneously.

posts.body:
## Cardiology Pairs

**STEMI vs Pericarditis:** STEMI = convex ST elevation, reciprocal changes, no PR depression. Pericarditis = concave ST elevation, PR depression, no reciprocal changes.

**Stable Angina vs MI:** Stable angina = exertional, relieved by rest/NTG, no enzyme rise. MI = rest pain, prolonged, enzyme rise.

**Atrial Fibrillation vs Atrial Flutter:** AF = irregularly irregular, no P waves, variable ventricular response. AFlutter = regular/sawtooth, flutter waves, usually 2:1 or 3:1 block.

## Medicine Pairs

**RA vs SLE:** RA = symmetric small joint, morning stiffness, rheumatoid factor, CCP. SLE = malar rash, ANA positive, dsDNA specific, multi-system.

**Addisons vs Cushings:** Addison = hypocortisolism, hyperpigmentation, hypotension. Cushing = hypercortisolism, central obesity, moon face, buffalo hump.

## Microbiology Pairs

**Typhoid vs Paratyphoid:** S. typhi = Widal positive, rose spots, ileal ulcers. S. paratyphi = milder disease, similar presentation.

## Surgery Pairs

**Appendicitis vs Mesenteric Adenitis:** Appendicitis = McBurney point tenderness, Rovsing sign, leucocytosis. Mesenteric adenitis = children, recent viral illness, diffuse pain.

posts.title: UPSC CMS Paper 1 vs Paper 2 Strategy: How to Allocate Time and Effort Across Both Papers
posts.description: UPSC CMS Paper 1 vs Paper 2 strategy — how to allocate study time, which subjects to prioritize, and how the two papers differ in difficulty and approach.
